segs.title: The age of Justinian
segs.text: Justinian the First reigned from 527 to 565. The Orthodox Church honors him as a saint and a theologian. He wanted one empire and one faith. He closed the pagan school of Athens in 529. His law code, the Code of Justinian, was issued in 534. He built Hagia Sophia in Constantinople, dedicated to Christ the Wisdom of God. In his day the Church was pictured as five great patriarchates: Rome, Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, and Jerusalem. Justinian called them the five senses of the universe. This order of five is called the pentarchy.

cards.q: When did the emperor Justinian the First reign?
cards.a: From 527 to 565.

cards.q: Name the five ancient patriarchates, the pentarchy.
cards.a: Rome, Constantinople, Alexandria, Antioch, and Jerusalem.

cards.q: What did Justinian call the five patriarchates?
cards.a: The five senses of the universe.

cards.q: What great church in Constantinople did Justinian build?
cards.a: Hagia Sophia, dedicated to Christ the Wisdom of God.

cards.q: What did Justinian do in 529, and what was issued in 534?
cards.a: In 529 he closed the pagan school of Athens. In 534 his law code, the Code of Justinian, was issued.

segs.title: The Three Chapters and the council
segs.text: Justinian longed to win back those who rejected Chalcedon. They suspected Chalcedon of leaning toward Nestorius. So Justinian condemned the Three Chapters: the person and writings of Theodore of Mopsuestia, the teacher of Nestorius, and the pro-Nestorian writings of Theodoret of Cyrrus and Ibas of Edessa. In 553 the Fifth Ecumenical Council met at Constantinople, from May 5 to June 2, with Patriarch Eutychius presiding. It condemned the Three Chapters and confessed Christ as one of the Holy Trinity, one divine person in two natures. It also condemned Origen and his later followers. Pope Vigilius opposed the council, then ratified it in February 554.

cards.q: In what year did the Fifth Ecumenical Council meet, and where?
cards.a: In 553, at Constantinople.
cards.ra: The Fifth Ecumenical Council met at Constantinople and condemned the Three Chapters and the errors of Origen.
cards.hook: Five, five, three: the Fifth council begins with two fives.

cards.q: What were the Three Chapters?
cards.a: The person and writings of Theodore of Mopsuestia, and the pro-Nestorian writings of Theodoret of Cyrrus and Ibas of Edessa.

cards.q: Why did Justinian want the Three Chapters condemned?
cards.a: To show the opponents of Chalcedon that the Church was not Nestorian, and so win them back.

cards.q: Besides the Three Chapters, whose teachings did the Fifth Council condemn?
cards.a: Origen and his later followers, including the ideas that souls existed before bodies and that all, even demons, will finally be saved.

cards.q: Who presided at the Fifth Council?
cards.a: Patriarch Eutychius of Constantinople.

cards.q: How did Pope Vigilius respond to the Fifth Council?
cards.a: He opposed it and stayed away, but ratified its decisions in February 554.

cards.q: What did the Fifth Council affirm with the phrase, one of the Holy Trinity?
cards.a: That Jesus Christ is one divine person, the Son of God, who united divinity and humanity in himself.

cards.q: On what dates did the Fifth Council sit?
cards.a: From May 5 to June 2, 553.

cards.q: How many Fathers attended the Fifth Council?
cards.a: Tradition counts 165. Modern lists give about 152.

cards.q: Did the Fifth Council issue disciplinary canons?
cards.a: No. Neither the Fifth nor the Sixth Council issued canons, which is why the Council in Trullo was later called.

cards.q: When is the feast of the Fathers of the Fifth Council?
cards.a: July 25.

segs.title: The sixth century West
segs.text: By 553 the opponents of Chalcedon had their own bishops, and the council did not bring them back. In the West, Pope Saint Gregory the Great guided Rome through the Lombard invasions and sent missionaries to England. He objected when Saint John the Faster of Constantinople took the title Ecumenical Patriarch. And in Spain, most likely at the Council of Toledo in 589, the words and the Son were added to the Creed, to stress the divinity of Christ to the Arian Visigoths. In Latin the addition is one word, filioque. The Orthodox hold that no local council may alter the Creed of the whole Church.

cards.q: Which patriarch of Constantinople first used the title Ecumenical Patriarch, and which pope objected?
cards.a: Saint John the Faster. Pope Saint Gregory the Great objected.

cards.q: Where and when was the filioque most likely first added to the Creed?
cards.a: In Spain, at the Council of Toledo in 589.

cards.q: Why was the filioque first added in Spain?
cards.a: To stress the divinity of Christ to the Arian Visigoths.

segs.title: One energy, one will
segs.text: In 610 Heraclius became emperor and Sergius became patriarch of Constantinople. They wanted to reunite the empire with those who rejected Chalcedon. Sergius offered a formula: in Christ there is one divine and human energy. This is Monoenergism. In 633 the elderly monk Sophronius, soon to be patriarch of Jerusalem, objected that it denied Christ a human energy. Sergius then proposed one will instead, and Pope Honorius of Rome agreed. This is Monothelitism. In 638 Heraclius proclaimed it by a decree called the Ekthesis.

cards.q: What is Monothelitism?
cards.a: The teaching that Christ has only one will.

cards.q: What is Monoenergism?
cards.a: The teaching that Christ has only one energy, or operation.

cards.q: Which emperor and patriarch promoted these teachings to reunite the empire?
cards.a: The emperor Heraclius and Patriarch Sergius of Constantinople.

cards.q: What was the Ekthesis, and when was it issued?
cards.a: The decree of the emperor Heraclius in 638 that proclaimed one will in Christ.

cards.q: Who first objected to Monoenergism, in 633?
cards.a: Saint Sophronius, who became patriarch of Jerusalem.

cards.q: Which pope accepted the formula of one will and was later condemned for it?
cards.a: Pope Honorius of Rome.

segs.title: Saint Maximus the Confessor
segs.text: Saint Maximus the Confessor lived from about 580 to 662. He had been secretary to the emperor Heraclius before he became a monk. He taught that each nature of Christ has its own will and energy. Christ has the divine will he shares with the Father and the Spirit, and a true human will like ours. He healed our will by freely submitting his human will to the divine. In 649 Pope Saint Martin held a council in Rome that condemned the new teaching. Both men were arrested, tried, and exiled. The tongue and right hand of Maximus were cut off. He died in exile in 662.

cards.q: Who was the chief theologian against Monothelitism, and when did he live?
cards.a: Saint Maximus the Confessor, from about 580 to 662.

cards.q: What did Saint Maximus teach about the wills of Christ?
cards.a: Christ has two wills, divine and human, because each nature has its own will and energy. He healed the human will by freely submitting it to the divine will.

cards.q: What happened in Rome in 649?
cards.a: Pope Saint Martin, inspired by Saint Maximus, held a council that condemned Monoenergism and Monothelitism.

cards.q: What did Saint Maximus suffer for his confession?
cards.a: He was tried and exiled, and his tongue and right hand were cut off.

cards.q: Where and when did Saint Maximus die?
cards.a: In exile in Lazica, in modern Georgia, on August 13, 662.

cards.q: Which emperor had Saint Maximus arrested?
cards.a: Constans the Second.

segs.title: The council
segs.text: The teaching of Sophronius, Maximus, and Martin won in the end. The emperor Constantine the Fourth called the Sixth Ecumenical Council. It met at Constantinople from November 7, 680, to September 16, 681. Pope Saint Agatho of Rome prepared the way. The council defined that Christ has two natural wills and two natural energies, divine and human. It condemned the patriarchs Sergius, Pyrrhus, Paul, and Peter of Constantinople, and it condemned Pope Honorius of Rome. The Church counts 170 Fathers and keeps their feast on January 23.

cards.q: In what years did the Sixth Ecumenical Council meet, and where?
cards.a: In 680 to 681, at Constantinople.
cards.ra: The Sixth Ecumenical Council met at Constantinople and condemned Monothelitism.
cards.hook: Six eighty for the Sixth council.

cards.q: Which emperor called the Sixth Ecumenical Council?
cards.a: Constantine the Fourth.

cards.q: What did the Sixth Council define?
cards.a: That Christ has two natural wills and two natural energies, divine and human.

cards.q: Whom did the Sixth Council condemn?
cards.a: The patriarchs Sergius, Pyrrhus, Paul, and Peter of Constantinople, and Pope Honorius of Rome.

cards.q: Which pope prepared the way for the Sixth Council?
cards.a: Pope Saint Agatho.

cards.q: On what dates did the Sixth Council sit?
cards.a: From November 7, 680, to September 16, 681.

cards.q: How many Fathers does the Church count at the Sixth Council, and when is their feast?
cards.a: 170. Their feast is January 23.

segs.title: Trullo and the rise of Islam
segs.text: The Fifth and Sixth Councils issued no canons. So in 692 the Eastern bishops met in the imperial palace in Constantinople, in the hall called Trullo. They issued 102 canons. This is the Council in Trullo, or Quinisext Council, meaning fifth-sixth. Canon 13 upheld the marriages of deacons and priests, against the Roman rule. Rome never accepted this council. Meanwhile the world had changed. The Muslim era is counted from 622, when Mohammed left Mecca for Medina. By 644 Arab armies held Egypt, Palestine, and Syria. Most of the Christians who rejected Chalcedon now lived under Muslim rule, cut off from the Byzantine Church.

cards.q: What was the Council in Trullo, and when did it meet?
cards.a: A council at Constantinople in 692 that issued 102 canons. It is also called the Quinisext Council.
cards.ra: The Council in Trullo, the Quinisext Council, issued 102 canons.

cards.q: Why is it called Quinisext, meaning fifth-sixth?
cards.a: Because its canons complete the Fifth and Sixth Councils, which issued none.

cards.q: What did canon 13 of Trullo uphold against Roman practice?
cards.a: The lawful marriages of deacons and priests.

cards.q: How do Rome and the Orthodox each regard the Council in Trullo?
cards.a: Rome never accepted it. The Orthodox give its canons the authority of an Ecumenical Council.

cards.q: What year marks the start of the Muslim era, and why?
cards.a: 622, when Mohammed left Mecca for Medina.

cards.q: Which lands did the Arab armies take from the Empire by 644?
cards.a: Egypt, Palestine, and Syria, along with Mesopotamia and Persia.

cards.q: How did the Arab conquests affect the division over Chalcedon?
cards.a: Nearly all the non-Chalcedonian Christians came under Muslim rule, which ended the hope of reunion with the Byzantine Church.

cards.q: Who wrote The Ladder of Divine Ascent?
cards.a: Saint John Climacus, abbot of Saint Catherine's Monastery on Mount Sinai.

title: Seventh Council: Nicaea, 787, and the Icons

segs.title: The breaking of images
segs.text: Iconoclasm means the breaking of images. The emperor Leo the Third saved Constantinople from an Arab siege in 717 to 718. Then, from 726, he issued edicts against the holy icons, calling them idols. Saint Germanus, patriarch of Constantinople, was deposed in 730 for refusing to go along. The great defender of the icons was Saint John of Damascus, a monk of Saint Sabas Monastery in Palestine, who died in 749. He taught that because God became man and was seen in the flesh, he can be depicted. Icons receive veneration, in Greek proskynesis. Worship, in Greek latreia, belongs to God alone.

cards.q: What does iconoclasm mean, and which emperor began it?
cards.a: The breaking of images. The emperor Leo the Third began it with edicts against icons from 726.

cards.q: Who was the great defender of icons in the first period of iconoclasm?
cards.a: Saint John of Damascus, a monk of Saint Sabas Monastery in Palestine.

cards.q: What is the main argument of Saint John of Damascus for icons?
cards.a: Because God became man and was seen in the flesh, he can be depicted.

cards.q: What distinction did Saint John of Damascus draw about honoring icons?
cards.a: Icons receive veneration. Worship belongs to God alone.

cards.q: Give the Greek words for veneration and for worship.
cards.a: Proskynesis is veneration. Latreia is worship.

cards.q: Which patriarch of Constantinople was deposed in 730 for refusing to reject icons?
cards.a: Saint Germanus.

cards.q: When did Saint John of Damascus die, and what are his main works?
cards.a: He died in 749. He wrote On the Holy Images and The Fount of Knowledge, which contains his Exposition of the Orthodox Faith.

segs.title: A false council and a true one
segs.text: Leo's son, Constantine the Fifth, was harsher. In 754 he gathered 338 bishops at Hieria, near Constantinople, in a council that condemned icons. The Church rejects it as a false council. From 762 to 775, the decade of blood, hundreds of monks were tortured or killed. Relief came through the empress Irene and Patriarch Tarasius. The Seventh Ecumenical Council opened at Nicaea on September 24, 787. Pope Hadrian the First sent legates and confirmed it. The council decreed that icons are to be displayed and venerated, but not given the worship due to God alone. It issued 22 canons. Canon 7 requires relics in every church.

cards.q: In what year did the Seventh Ecumenical Council meet, and where?
cards.a: In 787, at Nicaea.
cards.ra: The Seventh Ecumenical Council met at Nicaea and restored the veneration of icons.
cards.hook: Seven, eight, seven: the Seventh council begins and ends with seven.

cards.q: Which empress and patriarch brought about the Seventh Council?
cards.a: The empress Irene and Patriarch Tarasius of Constantinople.

cards.q: What did the Seventh Council decree?
cards.a: Icons are to be displayed and venerated, but not given the worship that belongs to God alone.

cards.q: What was the iconoclast council of 754?
cards.a: A council of 338 bishops at Hieria, near Constantinople, called by Constantine the Fifth, that condemned icons. The Church rejects it as a false council.

cards.q: On what date did the Seventh Council open, and how many bishops signed?
cards.a: September 24, 787. About 308 bishops signed, among roughly 350 members.

cards.q: How many canons did the Seventh Council issue, and what did canon 7 require?
cards.a: Twenty-two. Canon 7 required relics in every church.

cards.q: Which pope sent legates and confirmed the Seventh Council?
cards.a: Pope Hadrian the First.

cards.q: Why did Charlemagne's court attack the Seventh Council in the Libri Carolini?
cards.a: A faulty Latin translation blurred veneration with adoration, and Charlemagne wished to discredit the Eastern empire.

cards.q: What were the years of the decade of blood under Constantine the Fifth?
When does the Church commemorate the Fathers of the Seventh Council?
cards.a: On the Sunday nearest October 11.

segs.title: The Triumph of Orthodoxy
segs.text: Iconoclasm came back. In 815 the emperor Leo the Fifth, the Armenian, ordered the icons hung out of reach. On Palm Sunday of that year Saint Theodore the Studite, abbot of the Studion Monastery, led a procession with icons in open defiance, and was exiled. The persecution lasted until the emperor Theophilus died in 842. His widow, Saint Theodora, ruled for their young son Michael the Third. In March 843 Saint Methodius became patriarch, and on March 11, the first Sunday of Great Lent, the icons were carried back in procession. The Church keeps that day every year as the Sunday of Orthodoxy.

cards.q: What is the Triumph of Orthodoxy, and when did it happen?
cards.a: The final restoration of the icons on March 11, 843, the first Sunday of Great Lent.
cards.ra: The Triumph of Orthodoxy: the icons were restored for good under the empress Theodora.

cards.q: Which empress restored the icons in 843?
cards.a: Saint Theodora, regent for her son Michael the Third.

cards.q: When does the Church celebrate the Sunday of Orthodoxy?
cards.a: Every year on the first Sunday of Great Lent.

cards.q: Which emperor began the second period of iconoclasm, and in what year?
cards.a: Leo the Fifth, the Armenian, in 815.

cards.q: Who was the chief defender of icons in the second period?
cards.a: Saint Theodore the Studite, abbot of the Studion Monastery in Constantinople.

cards.q: Which patriarch was installed in March 843 to restore the icons?
cards.a: Saint Methodius, who had spent seven years in prison for the icons.

cards.q: Name the two empresses who ended the two periods of iconoclasm.
cards.a: Irene ended the first, and Theodora ended the second.

cards.q: Who wrote the Great Penitential Canon sung in Great Lent?
cards.a: Saint Andrew of Crete.
